axes.name: Democracy vs Autocracy
axes.description: Elected, accountable government versus concentrated rule.

axes.name: Authority vs Liberty
axes.description: State control, order, and security versus personal freedom and privacy.

axes.name: Assimilation vs Multiculturalism
axes.description: A shared national culture versus accommodating distinct cultural identities.

axes.name: Restricted Immigration vs Open Immigration
axes.description: Tighter immigration limits versus easier entry and settlement.

axes.name: Militarist vs Pacifist
axes.description: Reliance on military strength and force versus diplomacy and avoiding armed conflict.

axes.name: Nationalism vs Internationalism
axes.description: Prioritising national sovereignty versus sharing authority through international institutions.

axes.name: Public vs Private
axes.description: Government ownership versus private ownership of businesses and services.

axes.name: Protectionism vs Free Trade
axes.description: Protecting domestic industries versus reducing barriers to international trade.

axes.name: Planning vs Free Market
axes.description: Government direction of the economy versus decisions through markets and competition.

axes.name: High Redistribution vs Low Redistribution
axes.description: More redistribution through taxes and benefits versus letting people retain more of their income and wealth.

axes.name: Secular vs Religious
axes.description: Keeping religion separate from government versus giving it a role in law and public institutions.

axes.name: Progressive vs Traditionalist
axes.description: Changing social norms and institutions versus preserving established traditions.

axes.name: Innovation vs Caution
axes.description: Prioritising technological progress and development versus taking a cautious approach to protect people, biological systems, and the environment.

axes.name: Central vs Local
axes.description: Decisions made by central government versus regional and local institutions.

axes.name: Culture vs Nature
axes.description: Seeing human traits and behaviour as shaped mainly by society and upbringing versus biology and inherited characteristics.
